body_html:
Anniversary messages in Spanish can be as simple as ¡Feliz aniversario, mi amor! or as personal as a few lines about the years you have shared. Whether it is your first anniversary, your tenth or your parents’ fortieth, Spanish has warm, natural ways to celebrate it. Below are thirty-five anniversary messages to copy and adapt, grouped by occasion, with English translations and tips for cards and social media.

Quick answer
  • Basic: ¡Feliz aniversario!
  • Romantic: Gracias por estos años a tu lado.
  • For parents: ¡Feliz aniversario, papás! Gracias por enseñarnos lo que es el amor.
  • Dating anniversaries are often celebrated monthly by young couples: ¡Feliz mes!
{{toc}}

Short anniversary messages in Spanish

  1. ¡Feliz aniversario, mi amor!
    Happy anniversary, my love!
  2. Un año más a tu lado. ¡Feliz aniversario!
    One more year by your side. Happy anniversary!
  3. Contigo, cada año es mejor.
    With you, every year is better.
  4. Por muchos años más juntos.
    Here’s to many more years together.
  5. Gracias por elegirme cada día.
    Thank you for choosing me every day.
  6. Te amo hoy más que ayer.
    I love you more today than yesterday.

Romantic messages for your partner

  1. Hace un año empezó la mejor historia de mi vida.
    A year ago, the best story of my life began.
  2. Gracias por estos años llenos de risas, paciencia y amor.
    Thank you for these years full of laughter, patience and love.
  3. Si volviera a nacer, te elegiría otra vez.
    If I were born again, I would choose you again.
  4. Contigo aprendí que el amor se construye todos los días.
    With you I learned that love is built every day.
  5. No sé qué nos espera, pero sé que lo quiero vivir contigo.
    I don’t know what lies ahead, but I know I want to live it with you.
  6. Diez años después, todavía me pones nervioso.
    Ten years later, you still make me nervous.
  7. Eres mi hogar.
    You are my home.
  8. Feliz aniversario a la persona que hace que todo valga la pena.
    Happy anniversary to the person who makes everything worth it.

For longer, more personal writing, see {{link:love-letter-in-spanish|how to write a love letter in Spanish}}.

{{image:2}}

Wedding anniversary messages

  1. Feliz aniversario de bodas, mi vida.
    Happy wedding anniversary, my love.
  2. Cinco años de casados y sigo enamorada como el primer día.
    Five years married and I’m still as in love as on the first day.
  3. Gracias por cumplir cada promesa que me hiciste en el altar.
    Thank you for keeping every promise you made me at the altar.
  4. Volvería a decirte “sí, acepto” mil veces.
    I would say “I do” to you a thousand times.
  5. Por todo lo que hemos construido y todo lo que falta.
    Here’s to everything we’ve built and everything still to come.

Milestones have names in Spanish too: bodas de plata (silver, 25 years) and bodas de oro (golden, 50 years). For wedding-day phrases, see {{link:spanish-wedding-phrases|Spanish wedding phrases}}.

For your parents or another couple

  1. ¡Feliz aniversario, papás! Gracias por enseñarnos lo que es el amor.
    Happy anniversary, Mom and Dad! Thank you for showing us what love is.
  2. Felicidades por sus bodas de plata. ¡Que vengan muchos años más!
    Congratulations on your silver anniversary. Here’s to many more years!
  3. Su amor es un ejemplo para toda la familia.
    Your love is an example for the whole family.
  4. ¡Felicidades a la pareja más bonita!
    Congratulations to the loveliest couple!
  5. Que sigan celebrando juntos muchos años más.
    May you keep celebrating together for many more years.
  6. Cuarenta años juntos… ¡qué bendición!
    Forty years together… what a blessing!

Notice the plural ustedes forms (sus, sigan) when writing to a couple.

{{book:love-slowly}}

Funny anniversary messages

  1. Feliz aniversario a la única persona que aguanta mis chistes.
    Happy anniversary to the only person who puts up with my jokes.
  2. Un año más y todavía no sabemos qué cenar.
    One more year and we still don’t know what to have for dinner.
  3. Gracias por compartir la vida conmigo… y por dejarme la mitad de la cama. A veces.
    Thank you for sharing your life with me… and for leaving me half the bed. Sometimes.
  4. Feliz aniversario. Sigues siendo mi persona favorita para ignorar el resto del mundo.
    Happy anniversary. You’re still my favorite person to ignore the rest of the world with.

Monthly anniversaries and dating anniversaries

Many young couples in Latin America celebrate every month together, not just every year. You will see messages like:

  • ¡Feliz mes, mi amor! Happy month, my love!
  • Seis meses contigo y parece que te conozco de toda la vida. Six months with you and it feels like I’ve known you forever.
  • ¡Feliz primer aniversario de novios! Happy first dating anniversary!

A dating relationship is un noviazgo, and your boyfriend or girlfriend is tu novio or tu novia. For the early stages, see {{link:first-date-in-spanish|first date in Spanish}}.

{{image:3}}

Tips and common mistakes

  • Feliz cumpleaños for an anniversary. Cumpleaños is a birthday. An anniversary is aniversario.
  • Feliz aniversario de casados vs de bodas. Both are correct and common.
  • Años juntos without de. Say cinco años de casados (five years married) or cinco años juntos.
  • Copying a long poem. A short, personal sentence usually means more than a famous quote.

The RAE dictionary defines aniversario as the day on which a year is completed since an event. For birthdays, see {{link:birthday-wishes-in-spanish|birthday wishes in Spanish}}.

{{quiz}}

Final thoughts

The best anniversary messages in Spanish are short and personal. Start with one of the lines above, add a memory only the two of you share, and it will mean more than any poem. For more moments that matter, see {{link:spanish-phrases-for-everyday-situations|Spanish phrases for everyday situations}}.

faq.q: How do you say happy anniversary in Spanish?
faq.a: ¡Feliz aniversario! For a wedding anniversary, ¡Feliz aniversario de bodas!

faq.q: What do you write in an anniversary card in Spanish?
faq.a: A greeting, one or two personal lines about your time together, and a wish for the future, such as por muchos años más juntos.

faq.q: What are bodas de plata and bodas de oro?
Do couples celebrate monthly anniversaries in Latin America?
faq.a: Many young couples do, with messages like ¡Feliz mes, mi amor!

questions.q: To your parents (plural): “May you keep celebrating.”
“Thank you for choosing me every day.”
